title: A real city. A browser world.
label: TURKU / FINLAND
text: This is Turku, running in a browser. The streets begin as measurements. The buildings gain their character through generated facades. And beyond the detailed blocks, another pipeline builds the world as you move.

title: Two speeds of city building
label: DETAILED CORE + PROCEDURAL DRAFTS
text: The goal is a Grand Theft Auto style city, starting around Läntinen Rantakatu fifteen. Three dot J S draws it through Web G P U. Rapier handles physics in a worker.

title: Start with the laser returns
label: 01 / MEASURE THE CITY
text: First, the city's lidar. Every return records a measured position. Roofs, trees, and streets emerge from the point cloud. Classification separates ground samples from the objects standing above them.

title: Height must become collision
label: GROUND / STRUCTURES
text: Those ground samples become a surface. Cross sections help locate changes beside mapped street edges. Curbs and stairs need geometry and validation: a painted line cannot tell the physics engine where a step belongs.

title: The same office block, from above
label: 2022 TRUE ORTHOPHOTO → GAME
text: The twenty twenty two true orthophoto supplies ground colour. Here, the source image and the rendered office block share the same location. The image anchors the terrain to the real city.

title: Roofs already have a shape
label: CITY LOD2 + BUILDING REGISTER
text: City building models supply roof shapes. The detailed pipeline compares shells and reconstructed roofs against lidar. Building records give them persistent identities. Where evidence is insufficient, an explicit footprint extrusion provides a simpler fallback.

title: A map becomes a connected world
label: OPENSTREETMAP / LOCAL EXTRACT
text: OpenStreetMap contributes streets, tree points, barriers, and bridge tags. These become instructions for placement. Roads connect to their neighbours; fences follow the terrain; bridge decks need clearance beneath them.

title: What you see. What stops you.
label: 02 / BUILD THE DETAILED CORE
text: The detailed blocks combine separate ground, structure, and building layers. Visual meshes describe what you see. Collision meshes describe what stops you. Both come from the source data, with accuracy checked independently.

title: Generate → review → retry
label: GENERATED FACADE MAPS
text: Facades add recognisable character. An image model generates a wall map. A separate reviewer checks it, and failed candidates can be retried. Building styles and derived maps keep related walls consistent.

title: Local reference → parameters → facade
label: FAST PARAMETRIC PASS
text: Street panoramas are used only as local reference. None appear in this video. The faster pass describes a wall as parameters, then renders its colour, storeys, and window rhythm procedurally, without photograph pixels.

title: The space between the buildings
label: TREES / STREET FURNITURE / VEHICLES
text: Trees, street furniture, and parked cars fill the spaces between buildings. Placement checks surrounding geometry. Instancing reuses meshes, while vegetation changes its level of detail with distance.

title: 250 metres at a time
label: COMPRESSED GEOMETRY + TEXTURES
text: The assembler packages visual and collision tiles. The finest visual tiles span two hundred and fifty metres, with an eight megabyte wire budget. The browser streams a neighbourhood instead of the entire city.

title: Beyond the detailed core
label: 03 / LOCAL DRAFT GENERATION
text: Outside the published blocks, the local draft service builds simpler tiles from cached sources: coarse ground, orthophoto colour, extruded buildings, and a shared facade kit. These are procedural approximations, not surveyed replicas.

title: Build around you. Look ahead.
label: REQUEST AREA / SCHEMATIC OVERLAY
text: Requests follow the player. A five hundred metre ring covers the surroundings. A forward cone grows with speed, reaching one and a half kilometres at the car's top speed, fetching missing inputs first.

title: Fast geometry still needs data
label: RECORDED SERVICE BENCHMARK / 27 OCT 2026
text: A recorded westbound benchmark averaged three point four seconds per tile build. Dense southeast travel exposed the limit: downloads fell behind. Fast geometry does not make missing source data arrive instantly.

title: Drafts still have structure
label: BRIDGES / BARRIERS / VEGETATION
text: Draft producers interpret bridge decks, barriers, and wooded areas. Forest placement excludes roads, water, and buildings. The same system also builds tagged tunnels and passages, with solid walls, roofs, and floors.

title: Keep the world visible
label: LOAD → REPLACE
text: A ready replacement can swap into the running game while the current world stays visible during loading. Published detailed tiles replace drafts. Local development releases can update the scene without restarting the session.

title: Small changes. Fast feedback.
label: 04 / THE DEVELOPMENT LOOP
text: Behind the scenes, Codex tasks work in isolated sandboxes. Small commits pass the fast gate and land on main. The integrator builds and publishes; deeper browser and visual checks then report advisory failures.

title: From measured city to playable world
label: TURKU3D / WORK IN PROGRESS
text: Measure the city. Build its structure. Add character. Then stream and refine it. A detailed core and a faster outer world, meeting in one browser. Turku three D is still taking shape.
